The forward stroke is a rotation of the torso, not a pull of the arms.
Plant the blade near the foot, unwind the hips, and lift it out level
with the hip. The top hand stays loose; the power belongs to the torso
and the leg drive.

A short, quick cadence holds a loaded kayak on course better than a
long, slow one, because the boat is never allowed to yaw between
strokes. Set the stroke on one side against the boat's tendency to turn
and the paddle does the work a rudder would.

Bracing is the same movement with a flat blade: slap the surface, lean
into the support instead of fighting it, and let the hip carry the
weight. Anyone whose arms ache after an hour on flat sea is paddling
with the wrong muscles.
